sources.iso27001: ISO/IEC 27001:2022, Annex A. Control identifiers and titles as published by ISO/IEC.
sources.nistcsf: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (NIST CSWP 29, February 2024). Subcategory identifiers as published by NIST.
sources.cis: CIS Critical Security Controls v8.1 (Center for Internet Security). Safeguard numbering as published by CIS.
sources.rbi: Reserve Bank of India, 'Cyber Security Framework in Banks', circular DBS.CO/CSITE/BC.11/33.01.001/2015-16 dated 2 June 2016 (Annex 1 baseline requirements, Annex 2 C-SOC, Annex 3 CCMP). Internal RBI-A<n>-<nn> identifiers are this project's numbering; requirement substance follows the circular.
sources.sebi: SEBI, 'Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework (CSCRF) for SEBI Regulated Entities', circular SEBI/HO/ITD-1/ITD_CSC_EXT/P/CIR/2024/113 dated 20 August 2024, with the June 2025 FAQ and the 28 August 2025 technical clarifications. Internal SEBI-<FN>-<nn> identifiers are this project's numbering, grouped by the CSCRF's NIST CSF 2.0 anchoring.

meta.provenance_note: verification=verified means the identifier and title were checked against the published standard. inferred means the requirement substance is correct but the official clause numbering could not be confirmed from the primary document. assigned means this project created the identifier and records the basis for the mapping. Reports must surface this status; an inferred or assigned identifier is not a citation.

GV.RM-01.title: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders

GV.RM-02.title: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated and maintained

GV.RM-03.title: Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management processes

GV.RM-05.title: Lines of communication across the organization are established for cybersecurity risks

GV.RM-06.title: A standardized method for calculating, documenting, categorizing and prioritizing cybersecurity risks is established

GV.OV-01.title: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction

GV.OV-03.title: Organizational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed

GV.SC-04.title: Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality

GV.SC-07.title: The risks posed by a supplier, their products and services, and other third parties are understood, recorded, prioritized, assessed, responded to and monitored

ID.AM-01.title: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained

ID.AM-02.title: Inventories of software, services and systems managed by the organization are maintained

ID.AM-05.title: Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources and impact on the mission

ID.AM-08.title: Systems, hardware, software, services and data are managed throughout their life cycles

ID.RA-01.title: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated and recorded

ID.RA-02.title: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources

ID.RA-03.title: Internal and external threats to the organization are identified and recorded

ID.RA-04.title: Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities are identified and recorded

ID.RA-05.title: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritization

ID.RA-06.title: Risk responses are chosen, prioritized, planned, tracked and communicated

ID.RA-07.title: Changes and exceptions are managed, assessed for risk impact, recorded and tracked

ID.RA-08.title: Processes for receiving, analyzing and responding to vulnerability disclosures are established

ID.IM-02.title: Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises, including those done in coordination with suppliers and third parties

PR.AA-01.title: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services and hardware are managed by the organization

PR.AA-02.title: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions

PR.AA-03.title: Users, services and hardware are authenticated

PR.AA-05.title: Access permissions, entitlements and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced and reviewed, and incorporate the principle of least privilege

PR.AA-06.title: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored and enforced commensurate with risk

PR.AT-01.title: Personnel are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform general tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind

PR.AT-02.title: Individuals in specialized roles are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform relevant tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind

PR.DS-01.title: The confidentiality, integrity and availability of data-at-rest are protected

PR.DS-02.title: The confidentiality, integrity and availability of data-in-transit are protected

PR.DS-10.title: The confidentiality, integrity and availability of data-in-use are protected

PR.DS-11.title: Backups of data are created, protected, maintained and tested

PR.PS-01.title: Configuration management practices are established and applied

PR.PS-02.title: Software is maintained, replaced and removed commensurate with risk

PR.PS-03.title: Hardware is maintained, replaced and removed commensurate with risk

PR.PS-04.title: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring

PR.PS-05.title: Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented

PR.PS-06.title: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle

PR.IR-01.title: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage

PR.IR-02.title: The organization's technology assets are protected from environmental threats

PR.IR-03.title: Mechanisms are implemented to achieve resilience requirements in normal and adverse situations

PR.IR-04.title: Adequate resource capacity to ensure availability is maintained

DE.AE-02.title: Potentially adverse events are analyzed to better understand associated activities

DE.AE-03.title: Information is correlated from multiple sources

DE.AE-04.title: The estimated impact and scope of adverse events are understood

DE.AE-06.title: Information on adverse events is provided to authorized staff and tools

DE.AE-08.title: Incidents are declared when adverse events meet the defined incident criteria

DE.CM-01.title: Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events

DE.CM-03.title: Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events

DE.CM-06.title: External service provider activities and services are monitored to find potentially adverse events

DE.CM-09.title: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events

RS.MA-01.title: The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared

RS.MA-02.title: Incident reports are triaged and validated

RS.AN-03.title: Analysis is performed to establish what has taken place during an incident and the root cause of the incident

RS.CO-02.title: Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents

RS.CO-03.title: Information is shared with designated internal and external stakeholders

RC.CO-03.title: Recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities are communicated to designated internal and external stakeholders

sebi.name: SEBI CSCRF
sebi.long_name: SEBI Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework for Regulated Entities (circular SEBI/HO/ITD-1/ITD_CSC_EXT/P/CIR/2024/113, 20 August 2024)
sebi.authority: Securities and Exchange Board of India

SEBI-GV-01.title: Board-approved cybersecurity and cyber resilience policy
SEBI-GV-01.basis: CSCRF requires a board/partner/proprietor-approved policy reviewed at least annually.
SEBI-GV-01.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-GV-02.title: Designated senior official responsible for cybersecurity
SEBI-GV-02.basis: RE must designate a senior official (CISO or equivalent) accountable for the framework.
SEBI-GV-02.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-GV-03.title: Cyber Capability Index (CCI) measurement and reporting
SEBI-GV-03.basis: MIIs and Qualified REs must measure cyber resilience through the CCI; MIIs quarterly, Qualified REs annually.
SEBI-GV-03.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-GV-04.title: Third-party and outsourcing cyber risk governance
SEBI-GV-04.basis: Vendor/outsourcing arrangements must carry cybersecurity obligations and be assessed.
SEBI-GV-04.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-GV-05.title: Periodic cyber audit and submission to SEBI
SEBI-GV-05.basis: Cyber audits at the cadence set for the RE category, with findings reported to SEBI.
SEBI-GV-05.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-ID-01.title: Identification and classification of critical systems
SEBI-ID-01.basis: REs must identify critical systems and maintain a board-approved list.
SEBI-ID-01.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-ID-02.title: Asset inventory including hardware, software and data
SEBI-ID-02.basis: Comprehensive, current inventory of IT assets supporting critical systems.
SEBI-ID-02.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-ID-03.title: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for critical systems
SEBI-ID-03.basis: CSCRF introduces SBOM obligations for critical systems and new procurements.
SEBI-ID-03.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-ID-04.title: Risk assessment covering threats and vulnerabilities
SEBI-ID-04.basis: Documented risk assessment methodology linking threat, vulnerability and impact.
SEBI-ID-04.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-ID-05.title: Vulnerability assessment and penetration testing (VAPT)
SEBI-ID-05.basis: VAPT at the prescribed cadence, scoped to critical systems, with closure of findings and re-testing; reports submitted to SEBI.
SEBI-ID-05.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-PR-01.title: Access control and privilege management
SEBI-PR-01.basis: Least-privilege access, periodic review and removal of dormant privilege.
SEBI-PR-01.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-PR-02.title: Multi-factor authentication for critical access
SEBI-PR-02.basis: MFA required for access to critical systems and remote/administrative access.
SEBI-PR-02.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-PR-03.title: Network segregation and perimeter security
SEBI-PR-03.basis: Segregation of critical systems, controlled perimeter and secure configuration.
SEBI-PR-03.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-PR-04.title: Patch and vulnerability remediation management
SEBI-PR-04.basis: Timely patching with documented risk-based prioritisation of remediation.
SEBI-PR-04.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-PR-05.title: Data protection, encryption and data localisation
SEBI-PR-05.basis: Protection of data at rest and in transit; CSCRF sets expectations on storage of regulatory data within India.
SEBI-PR-05.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-PR-06.title: Secure software development and application security
SEBI-PR-06.basis: Security embedded in the application life cycle for RE-developed systems.
SEBI-PR-06.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-PR-07.title: Cybersecurity training and awareness
SEBI-PR-07.basis: Periodic training for employees and, where relevant, investors/customers.
SEBI-PR-07.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-DE-01.title: Security Operations Centre monitoring
SEBI-DE-01.basis: SOC coverage — own, group or market SOC — with continuous monitoring; smaller REs may use the SEBI-facilitated market SOC.
SEBI-DE-01.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-DE-02.title: Centralised logging and log retention
SEBI-DE-02.basis: Logs captured, protected and retained for the prescribed period.
SEBI-DE-02.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-DE-03.title: Continuous threat detection and alerting
SEBI-DE-03.basis: Detection capability with defined alert triage for critical systems.
SEBI-DE-03.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-RS-01.title: Incident response plan and containment procedures
SEBI-RS-01.basis: Documented, tested incident response covering containment and eradication.
SEBI-RS-01.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-RS-02.title: Incident reporting to SEBI and CERT-In within timelines
SEBI-RS-02.basis: Cyber incidents reported to SEBI and CERT-In within the stipulated timelines.
SEBI-RS-02.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-RS-03.title: Root cause analysis and forensic capability
SEBI-RS-03.basis: RCA and forensic readiness following significant incidents.
SEBI-RS-03.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-RC-01.title: Recovery, RTO/RPO objectives and business continuity
SEBI-RC-01.basis: BCP-DR with defined recovery objectives for critical systems and periodic drills.
SEBI-RC-01.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

SEBI-RC-02.title: Backup integrity and restoration testing
SEBI-RC-02.basis: Protected backups with tested restoration for critical systems.
SEBI-RC-02.note: Platform-assigned identifier; SEBI's official standard number unconfirmed.

vulnerability_classes.label: Remote code execution / command injection
vulnerability_classes.rationale: Unauthenticated code execution defeats application input validation and network containment simultaneously, so it is evidence against secure-development, network-protection and malware-defence controls at once.

vulnerability_classes.label: Untrusted deserialization
vulnerability_classes.rationale: Deserialization flaws almost always arrive through a third-party component, so they implicate component inventory and SBOM obligations as much as coding practice.

vulnerability_classes.label: SQL / NoSQL injection
vulnerability_classes.rationale: Injection into a datastore is both an application-security failure and a data-access-control failure, and the audit trail is what proves scope of exposure.

vulnerability_classes.label: Path traversal / unrestricted file upload
vulnerability_classes.rationale: Writing attacker-chosen files into a web root is the standard route to placing a web shell, which is why unauthorised-software controls appear here.

vulnerability_classes.label: Authentication bypass / missing authentication
vulnerability_classes.rationale: An authentication bypass is direct evidence that the authentication control objective is unmet, which is why multi-factor safeguards dominate the mapping.

vulnerability_classes.label: Broken access control / missing authorization
vulnerability_classes.rationale: Failure of least privilege. Reviewers will want the access-rights review evidence, not just the patch.

vulnerability_classes.label: Privilege escalation
vulnerability_classes.rationale: Escalation paths are governed by privileged-access controls; the detective mapping matters because escalation is usually only visible in privileged-activity logs.

vulnerability_classes.label: Memory corruption / buffer overflow
vulnerability_classes.rationale: Little can be done at configuration level, so the mapping leans on patching cadence and exploit-mitigation features rather than design controls.

vulnerability_classes.label: Hard-coded, weak or exposed credentials
vulnerability_classes.rationale: Credential weaknesses are the single most common precursor to account takeover, so phishing-resistant MFA is the control that actually closes the exposure.

vulnerability_classes.label: Cryptographic weakness / insecure transport
vulnerability_classes.rationale: Maps to cryptography and information-transfer controls; regulators treat cleartext handling of regulated data as a reportable control failure.

vulnerability_classes.label: Insecure default or misconfiguration
vulnerability_classes.rationale: Configuration drift is a baseline-hardening failure, and the asset inventory is what determines whether the drift was even detectable.

vulnerability_classes.label: Information disclosure / side channel
vulnerability_classes.rationale: Confidentiality-only impact, so the mapping is to classification and leakage controls rather than to availability or integrity objectives.

vulnerability_classes.label: Cross-site scripting / request forgery
vulnerability_classes.rationale: Client-side flaws are the delivery mechanism for phishing and session theft, which is why awareness and anti-phishing controls join the application mapping.

vulnerability_classes.label: Server-side request forgery / XML external entity
vulnerability_classes.rationale: SSRF converts an application flaw into lateral network reach, so segmentation is the compensating control a reviewer will look for.

vulnerability_classes.label: Vulnerable or untrusted third-party component
vulnerability_classes.rationale: The clearest place where SBOM obligations bite: you cannot report on component risk you have not inventoried.

vulnerability_classes.label: Denial of service / resource exhaustion
vulnerability_classes.rationale: Availability-only impact maps to capacity, resilience and recovery objectives — the controls that determine whether an outage becomes a reportable disruption.

vulnerability_classes.label: Race condition / time-of-check flaw
vulnerability_classes.rationale: Rarely caught by scanners, so the mapping points at security testing and penetration testing rather than at patch cadence.

vulnerability_classes.label: Ransomware / destructive malware exposure
vulnerability_classes.rationale: Ransomware is the case where recovery controls carry more of the residual-risk reduction than preventive ones, so backups are mapped as first-class evidence.

mitigation_classes.label: Network segmentation / zero-trust architecture
mitigation_classes.evidence: Segmentation policy, VLAN/ACL matrix, and evidence that east-west traffic is denied by default rather than merely monitored.

mitigation_classes.label: Phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication
mitigation_classes.evidence: Enrolment coverage by privilege tier, and the exception register for accounts still on password-only or SMS OTP.

mitigation_classes.label: Database activity monitoring and encryption at rest
mitigation_classes.evidence: Key-management procedure, cipher inventory, and DAM alert samples proving the monitoring is actually generating reviewable events.

mitigation_classes.label: Managed detection and response / XDR / SOC
mitigation_classes.evidence: Use-case coverage matrix, mean time to detect, and for RBI-regulated entities the C-SOC operating model. SEBI-regulated entities should also cite market-SOC or equivalent SOC onboarding.

mitigation_classes.label: WAF / IPS virtual patching
mitigation_classes.evidence: Rule coverage against the open finding list, and blocking-vs-monitoring mode per rule — a WAF in detect-only mode is not a compensating control.

mitigation_classes.label: Privileged access management / credential vaulting
mitigation_classes.evidence: Privileged account inventory, vaulting percentage, and the quarterly access recertification record.

mitigation_classes.label: Immutable, air-gapped backup and recovery
mitigation_classes.evidence: Last successful restore test with date and scope. Backup existence is not evidence; a tested restore is.

mitigation_classes.label: Patch and vulnerability management orchestration
mitigation_classes.evidence: Remediation-SLA attainment by severity band. This is the control most directly evidenced by the platform's own output, so the finding ageing report is the artefact to attach.

mitigation_classes.label: Network access control / 802.1X
mitigation_classes.evidence: Authenticated-port percentage and the count of unmanaged devices quarantined in the reporting period.

mitigation_classes.label: Security awareness and phishing simulation
mitigation_classes.evidence: Completion rates and, more usefully to a reviewer, the simulated-phishing click and report rates trended over time.

mitigation_classes.label: Governance, risk assessment and independent assurance
mitigation_classes.evidence: Board-approved policy with review date, latest VAPT report, and the risk register showing accepted residual risk with named owners. Has no CTRL- identifier in the sample scan because it is the layer the platform reports *into*, not a purchasable line item.

risk_metric_map.label: Expected annual loss
risk_metric_map.statement: Quantified financial consequence of the current open finding set, used to demonstrate that risk is assessed in business terms and against a stated appetite rather than by severity label alone.

risk_metric_map.label: Exploitation probability (model output)
risk_metric_map.statement: Threat-informed likelihood per finding. Evidences that prioritisation uses current threat intelligence and not just static CVSS severity.

risk_metric_map.label: Residual risk after planned mitigation
risk_metric_map.statement: The number a board must formally accept. Reporting it alongside the pre-treatment figure is what turns a scan into a risk-acceptance record.

risk_metric_map.label: Framework control coverage
risk_metric_map.statement: Proportion of mapped controls with at least one satisfying investment or no contradicting finding. This is the self-assessment percentage regulators ask for, and for SEBI-regulated entities it is the input to the Cyber Capability Index submission.

risk_metric_map.label: Critical and high finding count
risk_metric_map.statement: Open severe exposures at reporting date, with ageing. Directly evidences whether remediation timelines are being met.

risk_metric_map.label: Findings under active exploitation
risk_metric_map.statement: Count of findings matching a confirmed in-the-wild exploitation catalogue. Usually the single most escalation-worthy line in a board pack.

risk_metric_map.label: Return on security investment
risk_metric_map.statement: Risk reduction per rupee for the selected portfolio. Evidences that resourcing decisions are risk-based, which is a governance obligation in its own right and not merely a finance question.

risk_metric_map.label: Business-criticality weighted exposure
risk_metric_map.statement: Shows the asset inventory is classified and that risk is weighted by business impact — the precondition for every other number here being meaningful.
